newsitem.title: USA: Andrew Lloyd Webber musical opens in Washington.
newsitem.headline: Andrew Lloyd Webber musical opens in Washington.

text.p: Most premieres of musicals by blockbuster composers are greeted with a showy display of tuxes, celebrities, evening gowns and diamonds.

The world premiere here of Andrew Lloyd Webber's "Whistle Down the Wind" on Thursday night, however, simply featured wool-clad executives and Capitol Hill staffers -- just the low-key affair that Lloyd Webber wanted.

The Cajun-flavored, rock and gospel musical by Lloyd Webber received a strong response from the audience as the loudly cheering crowd gave the cast a long standing ovation at the conclusion of the nearly three-hour performance.
Members of the audience were enthusiastic, impressed by the cast, the music, the setting and the story.

"I'm enjoying it," government worker Valeria Conn said during the intermission. Conn had brought her 4-year-old granddaughter to the show, which many said appealed to children as well as to adults, particularly because of the number of kids in the cast.
"I definitely think it's a family show, something people of all ages can enjoy," said Patty Petrowski, a legal assistant.

Appropriate for Washington, D.C., the biggest celebrities in the house were former President George Bush and his wife Barbara. They sat across the aisle from Britain's Lloyd Webber, who shook hands with the former first couple before the opening notes.

Lloyd Webber and the "Whistle" staff had kept the show low profile, with publicity limited and local. Still, more than 90 percent of the tickets for the nine-week Washington run sold before the curtain went up on Thursday night.
"Whistle," set in Louisiana in 1959, is based on a 1960s-era novel and movie set in the north of England in which three children shelter a stranger in their barn, believing he is Jesus Christ.
Smaller in scale than his previous productions such as "Phantom of the Opera" and "Sunset Boulevard" and with few big names, the cast consists largely of children.
Female lead Irene Molloy, a recent high school graduate, made her professional debut in "Whistle" and was clearly overwhelmed by the enthusiastic audience.
Veteran Davis Gaines, who has played the role of the Phantom more times than any other actor, took the male lead opposite Molloy.
Lloyd Webber chose to open the musical in the U.S. capital rather than the more traditional London or New York because he thought it appropriate, given the show's American roots.
It is the first world opening of one of his shows outside Britain since "Jesus Christ Superstar" opened on Broadway in 1971.
The show is scheduled to hit Broadway on April 7.
